# Linux {.unnumbered}

A practical library for **Linux on the command line**, organized as a tree under this book:

```text
Linux
├── Commands          → topics (files, processes, networking, …) → individual commands
├── Editors           → vi, Neovim, tmux, … → chapter pages
└── Scripting
    └── Bash          → shells, scripting, variables, control, workbook
```

## Sidebar map

| Part | Sections include |
|------|------------------|
| **Commands** | Help & docs, files & paths, archives, processes, monitoring, users, networking, packages, services, … |
| **Editors** | Intro, vi/Vim/Neovim, nano, Emacs, Helix, Micro, tmux, Herdr, Zed, workflows |
| **Scripting → Bash** | Intro to shells, scripting basics, Bash features, variables, control, functions, workbook |

## How to use

1. Expand **Commands** → open a topic → open a command page.  
2. Expand **Editors** → pick an editor or workspace tool.  
3. Expand **Scripting → Bash** for shell programming and automation beyond one-liners.  
4. Use search when you already know the name.

## Conventions

- Ubuntu-first examples where package names matter.  
- Worked examples over option dumps.  
- Safety notes on destructive operations.

## Formats

HTML, PDF, and EPUB when built via the monorepo portal.
